body:
_Migrated from issue #1351, filed 2026-08-04._

Found by the v4.1.29 pre-tag refuter gate.

## Symptom

On an install with a custom read column **and more than one user**, one user reading a book
to the end in the browser marks that book Read for *everybody*.

OBSERVED (`config_read_column=4`, column empty, no `ReadBook` rows):

1. user `refuter2` (id 39) POSTs one `/ajax/bookmark/2/epub` with `percentage=99.5` → 201
2. `custom_column_4.value` → `1`
3. **admin**, a different user with no `ReadBook` row of their own, `GET /api/v1/books/2`
   → `{'read': True}`

Not reachable anonymously (anon POST → 302; the SPA route has `_require_real_user()`), but any
logged-in account triggers it.

## What is and isn't new

The *sharedness* is not new and is not a bug in itself: a Calibre custom column is book-level,
there is no per-user variant, and v4.1.28's own toggle already wrote it with no user filter
(`helper.py:871-877`). Any user's explicit "mark read" already affected everyone. kosync has
also written it on KOReader completion since #312.

What is new is the **trigger**. `cps/services/reading_position.py` (new in v4.1.29) routes the
web reader into `kosync.update_book_read_status`, which at
`kosync.py:518` does:

```python
if config.config_read_column and new_status == ub.ReadBook.STATUS_FINISHED:
    _mark_custom_read_column(book_id)
```

So shared state is now mutated **implicitly**, by a user who only read a book and never asked
to mark anything. Previously that took an explicit toggle click or a device sync.

## Why it's filed rather than reverted

Not writing the column would mean finishing a book in the browser doesn't show up at all on a
custom-column install — the #312 complaint, and the opposite of what #1316 is for. So the
question is what the *right* semantics are, not whether to back it out:

- accept it as the documented consequence of choosing a book-level column, or
- gate the implicit write (only mirror when the reading user is the only user, or when the
  column is already set), or
- keep per-user truth in `ub.ReadBook` and treat the column as a display mirror of the
  *acting* user only.

Related to the book-level/per-user asymmetry already noted in #1345, but that entry covers the
toggle direction; a new implicit writer isn't on it.
title: Finishing a book in the web reader marks it read for every user on a custom-read-column install
